claim: A durable user fact told in conversation (e.g. a birthday) is captured to the LIRF ledger, survives a restart, and is stated back EXACTLY when asked — with no hedge — because the Knowledge Spine binds the known fact and the verifier enforces it (regenerate under the hard binding contract, then a deterministic spine floor if the model still disclaims).
owner: anima/memory_lirf.py (Facts.capture/about/lookup, SELF), anima/spine.py (truth_class/is_known_fact/answer_from_fact/honest_unknown), anima/server.py (_turn capture + verifier ignored_known_fact enforcement), anima/organs/verifier.py

killer_test.name: birthday_survives_restart_stated_exactly
killer_test.setup: Turn 1: tell Vera a unique birthday ('my birthday is March 4th, 1991'); assert memory_lirf.capture wrote a durable fact and it is on disk in <name>.lirf.json. Simulate a restart: reload Facts(name) FRESH from disk (no re-telling). Turn 2: ask for the birthday. The bind/verify path must surface the KNOWN value (the MRI 'bind' frame shows a KNOWN truth-class binding); if the model hedges, the verifier regenerates under hard_bind and finally ships spine.answer_from_fact. Hermetic temp store; real .anima byte-unchanged.

known_gaps: The honest-UNKNOWN inverse must stay intact: a genuinely-unknown trait must still get 'I don't have that yet' + an ask, never a confabulated value. The cert should pair the killer test with a negative (ask for a fact never told -> honest unknown, no fabrication).
